The bug is in an added line, `gaussSeidelSingleBlock`, line 200 of gsSmoother.cpp:

```cpp
Dblock.block(i,0,1,size) = A.block(DoFs(i), DoFs(i)-i, 1, size);
```

**What block it actually builds.** Block Gauss-Seidel needs the diagonal block `Dblock(i,j) = A(DoFs(i), DoFs(j))`. This line instead copies the `size` columns starting at `DoFs(i)-i` in row `DoFs(i)`, so it fills in `Dblock(i,j) = A(DoFs(i), DoFs(i)-i+j)`. The two only match when the DoFs are consecutive, meaning `DoFs(i) = DoFs(0)+i`.

**Non-consecutive blocks are meant to be supported:**
- The header says each `blockInfo` entry is "a vector with the indices of the DoFs" in one block, with no requirement that they be consecutive.
- The function sorts whatever indices it is given.
- The commit message says the goal is to create "different blocking patterns". Yet it only claims testing on "chronological" blocks, which is the one case where this line works.

**Example.** Take `DoFs = {0, 2}` on the 1D Laplacian, the tridiagonal matrix with 2 on the diagonal and -1 next to it:
- The correct block is `[[A00, A02], [A20, A22]] = [[2, 0], [0, 2]]`.
- The code builds `[[A00, A01], [A21, A22]] = [[2, -1], [-1, 2]]`.

So `x_b += Dblock⁻¹ r_b` is not block Gauss-Seidel at all. It applies the inverse of a matrix unrelated to the block, so the smoother can stall or diverge. If that wrong block happens to be singular, `Dblock.inverse()` produces inf/NaN, which gets written straight into `x`. Nothing is asserted or reported, so the wrong results go unnoticed.

**Memory-safety side effect.** The same `DoFs(i)-i` offset can go negative if a block lists the same DoF twice, for example `{0, 0}` gives a starting column of -1. In release builds that reads outside the sparse matrix's storage, because `GISMO_ASSERT` is compiled out under `NDEBUG` (gsDebug.h:86). The only check, on the largest index, is also debug-only.

**Suggested fix:** fill the block element by element, e.g. `for (j…) Dblock(i,j) = A.coeff(DoFs(i), DoFs(j));`. That is correct for any set of indices and has no offset arithmetic to go out of range.

I found two bugs in the new default implementations in `src/gsCore/gsFunctionSet.hpp`. Both are in lines this commit adds, and both cause wrong behaviour or out-of-bounds access when the code runs.

**1. The default `active_into` returns an empty matrix (line 34).**
`result.setConstant(0,u.cols());` is meant to do what the comment says: "a single function 0 is active always", i.e. return a 1×N matrix of zeros. `gsConstantBasis::active_into` does exactly that with `result.setZero(1,u.cols())`.
- With two arguments, Eigen picks the vector-only overload `setConstant(Index size, const Scalar& value)`. That calls `resize(0)` with `u.cols()` as the fill value.
- G+Smo defines `EIGEN_NO_STATIC_ASSERT` (`gsConfig.h.in:96`), so this still compiles. The "vector method on a matrix" check becomes a runtime `eigen_assert`.
- In debug builds that assertion aborts the program.
- In release builds the result is resized to 0×1 with a null data pointer, and nothing is filled in.

This is the default for every `gsFunction` and `gsGeometry`, since none of them override `active_into`. It is reached through the new public `active()` / `active_into()` and through `compute(...)` / `computeMap(...)` with `NEED_ACTIVE`. Callers end up with no active indices. Any code that reads `actives(0,p)` or `out.active(p)` then reads through an empty or null buffer.

**2. `compute(const gsMapData<T>&, gsFuncData<T>&)` reads past the end of `values` (line 164).**

- `out.values[1]` is then an out-of-bounds `std::vector` access. That is undefined behaviour and a heap over-read. Under MSVC debug iterators it fails with "vector subscript out of range".
- Values-only is the most basic request, so this path is easy to hit.

**Smaller problems in the same new code (secondary):**
- In `compute(const gsMatrix<T>&, gsFuncData<T>&)` (line 140), a request for only `NEED_ACTIVE` makes `maxDeriv()` return -1. The default `evalAllDers_into` then throws `GISMO_ERROR`, so the actives-only branch a few lines later can never succeed on its own.
- At lines 171–173, `fundForm(p)` returns a view of size target dimension × domain dimension. `fform * grads` is then written back into a view of size domain dimension × number of gradients. votes.reasoning:
The change makes boundary vertices C0, but the constraint it uses is wrong whenever two or more faces meet at a boundary vertex. That case is every vertex along a straight mesh boundary.

**The corner is tied to the inner points**
- The new code sets a boundary-vertex corner to the average of the inner (1,1) points of the faces around it. That average only gives the right corner when faces surround the vertex on all sides, which is true only for interior vertices.
- **Typical case:** a boundary vertex v shared by two faces A and B. Phase 3 already maps the first point on their shared edge to 0.5·(A's (1,1) at v + B's (1,1) at v). The new corner row has exactly the same two entries. So in every basis function the corner equals that edge point, and every function in the space has zero slope along the interior edge at v.
- **Example:** take a flat grid with v=(0,0), A=[-1,0]×[0,1], B=[0,1]×[0,1] and N=5. The inner points sit at (∓0.25, 0.25), so the corner is forced to (0, 0.25) instead of (0, 0). The space can no longer represent u = y, or the geometry itself, near the boundary. That distorts `smooth_b` (L2 projection of the geometry) and `fit_function_b`.
- **Contradicts `smooth()`:** the existing `smooth()` (lines ~982–1000) uses a different C1 rule at boundary vertices. There the corner is a free point with its boundary-edge neighbours in line with it (P5 = 2·P0 − P1). The average of the inner points equals the shared-edge point P3, not the corner.

**Dirichlet regression in `laplace_beltrami`**
- `laplace_beltrami` is what `freeform_pde` calls. For a mapped basis, `gsFeSpace::setup` finds each side's boundary DOFs with `mapb->basis(p).boundary(side)`. That call (`gsMappedSingleBasis::boundaryOffset` → `sourceToTarget`) returns every global DOF with a nonzero weight in that side's local rows, with no threshold.
- A boundary corner's row now contains interior inner-point DOFs from every patch at that vertex. `markBoundary` therefore eliminates those interior DOFs, and the homogeneous BC fixes them to 0.
- Combined with the zero slope above, this clamps both the value and the slope at every boundary vertex and removes real interior unknowns, so the solution near the boundary is over-constrained.
- The removed guard existed to prevent exactly this: "eliminate them directly via markBoundary without touching interior global DOFs". The new comment makes the same claim for corners with one face, but the two-or-more branch now does touch interior DOFs.

The old code wasn't C0 at boundary vertices for projection or fitting, but that problem was already there. Under Dirichlet its per-patch corner DOFs were removed cleanly and the result was correct, so this change makes the PDE path worse.

**Suggested fix:** give each boundary vertex one shared free global DOF (allocated once per vertex, e.g. with a `std::map<Vertex, index_t>`) and map every patch corner at that vertex to it. That gives C0 without tying corners to inner points, and `markBoundary` then only touches boundary DOFs. Alternatively, use the boundary-edge rule from `smooth()`.

The `MESH_DIM` change in the example is unrelated.

The new explicit instantiations in `gsBoehm_.cpp` cause a defect that is easy to point to: one of them can't be built, and another puts broken removal logic into the library.

**1. The `gsTensorKnotRemove` instantiation (lines 233–241) breaks the library build.**
- The cmake script `gismoUse.cmake` compiles every `*_.cpp` into the library, so this file is always built.
- The instantiation forces the compiler to build the `.hpp` body with `str` as a `gsVector<index_t>`. That body passes `str`, `new_str` and `last_point` to `bspline::getLastIndex`, `getIndex` and `correctNewStride`. All three take `gsVector<unsigned>`, and `getLastIndex` also needs a `gsVector<int>&`.
- `correctNewStride(new_str, str, direction, -1)` has no overload that fits: a `gsVector<int>` variable can't be passed as a `gsVector<unsigned>&`.
- `getLastIndex(str, …)` would need to convert int to unsigned through gsVector's template constructor. Eigen rejects that at compile time with its mixed-numeric-types static assert.

**2. Even if it compiled, the exported function doesn't match the header.**
- The instantiation has the signature `index_t (…, index_t, gsVector<index_t>, index_t, bool)`.
- `gsBoehm.h` declares `int gsTensorKnotRemove(…, int, gsVector<unsigned>, int, bool)`.
- In library builds, callers only see the header, so they would need the `gsVector<unsigned>` version, which nothing instantiates. That means an undefined symbol at link time.
- `gsKnotRemove` has the same problem whenever `GISMO_INDEX_TYPE` isn't `int`. The docker CI build scripts list `int64_t`, `long` and `long long` variants: the header declares an `int t` version, but the library exports an `index_t t` one.

**3. The `gsKnotRemoveSingle` instantiation exports wrong logic.**
- The loop `while (ii <= jj)` always ends with `j < i`, so the "middle point" check is never reached.
- When p − s is even, the last loop step writes `temp[m+1]` twice, and the check then compares `temp[m+1]` with itself. The function therefore reports any such knot as exactly removable.
- The gap is also closed by dropping `coefs[last]` instead of the point at index (first+last)/2, as Algorithm A5.8 does. This shifts the right-hand new points by one.
- Linear example: knots `[0,0,.5,1,1]`, coefficients `(0,1,0)` (a hat). It returns `true` and gives `(0,0)`, which is the zero function.
- Cubic example: a Bézier with points `(0,1,3,2)`, with knot 0.5 inserted, has coefficients `(0,.5,2,2.5,2)`. Removing 0.5 is exact here, but the result is `(0,1,2,2)` instead of `(0,1,3,2)`.
- `gsTensorKnotRemove`, `gsBSpline::removeKnot`, `squared()` and `cubed()` all rely on this function, so they would silently produce wrong splines.
